h1:
Bangkok-Sa Kaeo-Siem Reap
Explore Sa Kaeo Before You Cross to Angkor
intro: Plenty of people race through Sa Kaeo just to cross the border to Angkor as fast as they can, but if you have an extra half-day to a full day, Aranyaprathet and Sa Kaeo town have more going for them than you'd expect: the biggest border market in eastern Thailand, thousand-year-old Khmer temples, and Vietnamese food that locals here actually do well. We've laid this out as a 3-day, 2-night trip leaving Bangkok, spending a night in Aranyaprathet, covering Sa Kaeo, then crossing over to Siem Reap — and we'll tell you straight what you need to check first. The Thai-Cambodian border situation in late 2025 to early 2026 has seen on-and-off closures, so before you actually travel you must always confirm the status of the Khlong Luek-Poipet crossing and your visa paperwork.

blocks.html: The Bangkok-Aranyaprathet-Poipet route is the overland gateway Thais have long used to reach Angkor, because it's only about 150 kilometres from the Khlong Luek border to Siem Reap — drive or catch onward transport for roughly another two and a half hours and you're there. But the thing people usually miss is rushing across the border without stopping for anything in Sa Kaeo at all, even though Aranyaprathet has Rong Kluea Market and good Vietnamese food, and the area around town still has Khmer temples and some unusual scenery to see. So this plan is built to let you do both.

blocks.text: How to get from Bangkok to Aranyaprathet

blocks.html: You've got three main options, depending on whether you want to save money, go fast, or travel in comfort. Bangkok to Aranyaprathet is about 250 kilometres — roughly three and a half hours by car if traffic is light.

items: Van/bus (fastest and most frequent) — These leave Mo Chit 2 terminal for Rong Kluea Market/Aranyaprathet, running from the early morning around 04:00 right through to evening. Tickets are about 230 THB and the trip takes 3.5-4 hours. Good if you're heading straight for Rong Kluea Market.

Train (cheap and full of atmosphere) — A third-class service leaves Krung Thep Aphiwat station in the early morning (around 05:55) and runs all the way to Ban Khlong Luek station right next to the border, arriving around midday. Fares start at a few tens up to just over a hundred baht. The upside is the last stop is a short walk from the border; the downside is it's slower than the van and there are only a few services a day.

Driving yourself (most flexible) — Take Suwannason Road (Highway 33), stopping at petrol stations and for food along the way. This is best if you plan to visit Sdok Kok Thom temple or Lalu, which sit outside town — public transport doesn't reach those spots.

blocks.title: Which one should you pick
blocks.html: If you want to make the most of Sa Kaeo before crossing, we'd suggest driving yourself or renting a car, since several of the standout sights are outside the town centre with no public transport. If you're only here to cross the border, the van straight to Rong Kluea Market is the most convenient.

blocks.text: The 3-day, 2-night timeline — Bangkok, Sa Kaeo, Siem Reap

blocks.html: This plan leaves enough time to actually explore Sa Kaeo rather than just pass through. Day one is travel and Aranyaprathet, day two covers the temples and scenery around town with another overnight, and day three you cross to Siem Reap in the morning so you reach Angkor in time for the afternoon. Add or drop days to fit the time you have.

items.note: Catch a van from Mo Chit 2 or the morning train / if driving, head out a bit early to beat the outbound traffic

items.activity: Arrive in Aranyaprathet, check in and drop your bags
items.note: Lodging in Aranyaprathet town ranges from budget guesthouses to riverside resorts, starting around 450-900 THB/night
The biggest border trade market in eastern Thailand — second-hand goods, clothes, bags, dried goods, and you can haggle. Stock changes constantly, so allow 2-3 hours to wander
Aranyaprathet has a long-established Vietnamese community, so naem nueang, fresh spring rolls and Vietnamese kuai chap are the real deal. Look for the places locals queue at

items.activity: Rest / find a cafe to chill
items.note: There are small cafes in town to escape the afternoon sun. Save your energy for the next day
Try moo kratha or a local made-to-order spot. Overnight in Aranyaprathet tonight

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Khmer temples + nature around Sa Kaeo

items.note: Rice soup, congee, or old-style coffee at the morning market, then head out of town

items.activity: Sdok Kok Thom temple, Khok Sung district
items.note: The largest Khmer temple in eastern Thailand, thought to date to around the 9th century AD. It's been restored and is easy to walk around, with a visitor centre that helps you understand the history
A temple on a small hill in the Aranyaprathet area, with a view and a different style of Khmer art. There's a short flight of steps to climb here
Find a spot along the route to refuel before the next nature stop

An earth formation where water and wind have eroded the soil into columns and cliffs, like a miniature Phae Mueang Phi. It's at its best in late rainy season to early winter; if you come in the rainy season the access road can be tough, so check road conditions first

items.activity: Back into Aranyaprathet for dinner and rest
items.note: Overnight in Aranyaprathet again. Get your documents and bags ready to cross the border early tomorrow

blocks.title: Lalu or Pang Sida — your call
blocks.html: If you prefer hiking and waterfalls over unusual earth formations, you can swap day two for Pang Sida National Park instead — it has waterfalls and butterfly-watching trails in early rainy season. But Pang Sida is in the opposite direction from the border, so plan your driving time carefully.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Cross the Khlong Luek-Poipet border → Siem Reap-Angkor Wat

items.note: Crossing the border in the morning means fewer people and more time left to explore the Siem Reap side

items.activity: Reach Khlong Luek border, get your Thai exit stamp
items.note: Have a passport with more than 6 months' validity and your Cambodia visa/e-Arrival paperwork ready. Always check the border status in advance

items.activity: Cross to the Poipet side, process your Cambodia entry
items.note: Watch out for touts offering to push you through the queue or overpriced services. Follow the official signs and don't rush to pay anyone
There are shared buses and private taxis. It's about 150 km and takes roughly 2.5 hours. Always agree the price before you get in

items.activity: Arrive in Siem Reap, check in, lunch
items.note: Change some riel/have dollars ready, and buy your Angkor Pass for an afternoon-evening visit
Late afternoon the sun softens, good for photos and walking the main temple, then on to sunset if you're up for it

blocks.text: Paperwork and border details to check before you actually go

blocks.html: This is the most important part of the whole plan, and it's the part that can change fast. From late 2025 into early 2026 there have been tensions along the Thai-Cambodian border, leaving several overland crossings — including Khlong Luek-Poipet — temporarily closed or with restricted entry and exit at times. Before you commit to a travel plan, always check the latest crossing status from official sources. Don't rely on old information.

items: Check the latest border status — Look at announcements from the immigration checkpoint/the Cambodian embassy in Thailand on whether the Khlong Luek crossing is open to tourists on the day you plan to go. If it's closed, the alternative is flying directly into Siem Reap or Phnom Penh instead.
Passport — It must have at least 6 months' validity from your entry date and enough blank pages for stamps.

Visa/arrival card — Tourists need to sort out a Cambodia visa and fill in Cambodia's e-Arrival under whatever system is in place at the time (requirements vary by nationality, so check your own carefully).
Cash — The Cambodian side runs mainly on US dollars alongside riel, so carry small bills. Poipet-Siem Reap transport runs roughly 9 USD by bus and around 12 USD per person by taxi.

Watch for scammers at the border — People will offer to help with your visa/push you through the queue at inflated prices. Do the paperwork yourself at the official window and ask the price before using any service.

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: We've written this plan as a route-skeleton guide, not a guarantee that the border will be open on the day you go. The border situation can change week to week. If the crossing is closed, flip to a Sa Kaeo-only trip or fly into Siem Reap instead — that's far safer.

Aranyaprathet's strength is Vietnamese food, thanks to a Vietnamese community that settled here long ago, so the flavours are closer to the original than in many towns. Beyond that there's border food and street food to keep trying as you go.

items.name: Naem nueang
items.blurb: Grilled minced pork wrapped in rice paper with fresh vegetables and rice noodles, dipped in a thick peanut sauce. Several Aranyaprathet shops nail the flavour

items.name: Vietnamese kuai chap
items.blurb: Clear, chewy-soft noodles in a light broth with pork, egg and fried shallots — a breakfast people around here genuinely eat

items.name: Fresh/fried spring rolls
items.blurb: Wrapped with fresh vegetables and pork, or fried until crisp — easy to snack on before your main meal

items.name: Food inside Rong Kluea Market
items.blurb: As you shop you'll find border snacks, fruit and sweets to refuel along the way

blocks.html: Aranyaprathet is a border town, so there's a wide range of accommodation at friendly prices — from guesthouses near the train station and daily-rate rooms to riverside resorts. Most sit in town and near Rong Kluea Market, making the onward trip to the border easy. Picking somewhere close to the border for your last night makes an early crossing simpler.

items: Near Rong Kluea Market/the border — Convenient if you plan to shop and cross early.
In Aranyaprathet town — Close to the Vietnamese restaurants and cafes, easy for eating and wandering on foot.
Riverside resort on the outskirts — Quieter, good if you want a proper rest before tackling the border crossing.

faq.q: How long does it take to get from Bangkok to Aranyaprathet?
faq.a: It's about 250 kilometres, roughly 3.5 hours by car if traffic is light. A van from Mo Chit 2 takes around 3.5-4 hours with tickets at about 230 THB. The third-class train from Krung Thep Aphiwat station leaves in the morning and reaches Ban Khlong Luek station around midday — slower, but cheaper and it drops you right by the border.

faq.q: Is it far from the Poipet border to Siem Reap?
faq.a: About 150 kilometres, roughly two and a half hours of onward travel. There are shared buses (around 9 USD per person) and private taxis (around 12 USD per person). Always agree the price before getting in.

faq.q: Can you cross the Khlong Luek-Poipet border right now?
faq.a: From late 2025 into early 2026 there have been Thai-Cambodian border tensions, leaving several overland crossings — including Khlong Luek-Poipet — temporarily closed and with restricted entry and exit at times. Before you go you must always check the latest crossing status from official sources. If it's closed, the alternative is flying into Siem Reap or Phnom Penh instead.

faq.q: What paperwork do you need before crossing into Cambodia?
faq.a: A passport with at least 6 months' validity and blank pages, a Cambodia visa, and a completed e-Arrival under whatever system is in place at the time. Requirements vary by nationality, so check your own carefully, and carry small US-dollar bills for the Cambodian side.

faq.q: If you only have half a day in Sa Kaeo, where should you stop?
faq.a: If time is short and you don't have your own car, walking Rong Kluea Market and eating Vietnamese food in Aranyaprathet is enough to soak up the border-town feel. Sdok Kok Thom temple and Lalu are outside town and need a car and more time.
